Plot health metrics for admin level 1 units

Source: R/plot.health_system.R
plot.cd_health_system_metric.Rd

Plots individual health system indicators by admin level 1 and compares with national value or target.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cd_health_system_metric'
plot(
  x,
  indicator = c("ratio_fac_pop", "ratio_hos_pop", "ratio_bed_pop", "ratio_hstaff_pop",
    "skill_mix"),
  national_value = NA_real_,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  x_title = NULL,
  y_title = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  ...,
  legend_labels = NULL,
  options = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Data frame containing admin level 1 indicators.

indicator

A single metric to plot. Options include ratio_fac_pop, ratio_hos_pop, ratio_bed_pop, ratio_hstaff_pop, skill_mix.

national_value

A numeric value representing the national average to plot as a vertical line. Can be NA.

title

The chart's title.

subtitle

The line under the title.

caption

The note under the chart.

x_title

The title of the horizontal axis.

y_title

The title of the vertical axis.

legend_title

The title of the legend.

...

Chart options by name (see cd_chart_options()): background, fonts, sizes, axes, grid, legend, colours. Other arguments are ignored.

legend_labels

(Optional) A named list to override default legend labels (e.g. for translation).

options

A cd_chart_options() object or a list of chart options: a look made once, to give to several charts. Applied after the text arguments, so a text it holds wins over them.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

cache <- load_cache_data(system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core"))
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths,
#>   ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
cache$adjust_data()
regions <- cache$health_system_metrics_admin1
national <- cache$health_system_metrics_national

plot(regions, indicator = "ratio_fac_pop", national_value = national$ratio_fac_pop)

plot(regions, indicator = "ratio_hstaff_pop", national_value = national$ratio_hstaff_pop,
     title = "Health workers per 10,000 people", x_title = "Health workers",
     legend_labels = list(threshold_line = "Benchmark (44.5)"))
